status_rubric.proposed_rubric: Status records how far the attack has been run against the real thing, not how plausible it is. THEORETICAL: no attack has been run against real neural data, a real decoder or real interface hardware; this covers arguments by analogy from attacks shown only on non-neural systems, review or taxonomy proposals, and simulation-only work, including in-silico tissue models and defence papers that assume the attack (label these 'modelled'). EMERGING: an attack has been run against real neural data, models or devices, but the evidence stops short of DEMONSTRATED because it is preprint-only, or its results are mixed or weak, or only parts of the path are shown (for example the coupling is shown for a benign purpose, or the delivery and the effect are shown separately). DEMONSTRATED: at least one peer-reviewed study with a Crossref-resolvable DOI or a PMID ran the attack and measured a clear positive result, and the entry states the evidence level; dataset-level evidence (offline recordings, digital perturbation) qualifies only when the technique's target is the model or the stored data, while a technique that claims a physical or live-system path needs hardware or participant evidence. CONFIRMED: DEMONSTRATED plus independent peer-reviewed replication by a second group on hardware or participants, or documented occurrence in a shipped product or in the field; it cannot be reached from preprints, simulations or dataset-only studies. In every case the label describes the attack, so a well-replicated clinical phenomenon does not by itself make its adversarial use CONFIRMED.

proposed_entry.attack: Harvest-now-decode-later (inferential re-analysis of retained neural recordings)
sources: Bagley B-A, Rose N, Kilbourn Q, Canham M. 2026. Threat Vectors and the State of the Art in Defense Methods for Security in Neurotechnology. arXiv:2607.10451v1 (review, preprint), section 2.1.2

Menuet R, Meudec R, Dockès J, Varoquaux G, Thirion B. 2022. Comprehensive decoding mental processes from Web repositories of functional brain images. Scientific Reports 12:7050. DOI:10.1038/s41598-022-10710-1 (non-adversarial; group-level fMRI statistical maps from an open repository; context for the enabling capability only)
proposed_entry.notes: Retain or acquire neural recordings now and apply later, more capable decoding models to extract inferences that cannot be obtained when the data is collected. No key is broken: the risk horizon is set by progress in decoding models, not by quantum hardware, so post-quantum cryptography (the control for QIF-T0045) does not address it. PROJECTED for BCI data: no incident or adversarial demonstration was found. Bagley et al. 2026 (section 2.1.2, review, preprint) describe the variant. Menuet et al. 2022 show, non-adversarially and on group-level fMRI statistical maps from an open repository, that archived neuroimaging data can be decoded by models trained later; that is not a result about individuals' retained recordings. Applicable controls are governance-side: retention limits, purpose limitation and deletion, not wire-protocol cryptography.

tara.mechanism: Retention of neural recordings for later re-analysis with decoding models that did not exist at collection time, yielding inferences beyond the scope known or consented to at collection

governance.safety_ceiling: Retention period and permitted re-analysis fixed at collection; deletion or renewed consent before any new decoding purpose. PQC does not mitigate this variant (no key is broken)

parameters.threat_horizon: bounded by decoding-model progress (not quantified in the source)
parameters.data_state: at rest: lawfully retained or previously exfiltrated

engineering.detection: Not observable at the device once data has left it; controls are retention audits, access logging and purpose-limitation enforcement at the data holder

proposed_entry.attack: VR headset motion-sensor inference of EEG-correlated responses (IMU capture of pupil-linked vibration)
sources: Ni T, Sun Z, Zhao Q, Lee W-B, Wang C. 2026. When VR Meets BCI: (Un)Observable Brainwave-Aware Privacy Reconstruction in the Metaverse via Unrestricted Inbuilt Motion Sensors. 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP), pp. 961-979. DOI:10.1109/SP63933.2026.00117
proposed_entry.notes: Accelerometer and gyroscope data that VR applications can read without a sensor permission capture small headset vibrations linked to the wearer's pupillary responses. Ni et al. 2026 (IEEE S&P, peer reviewed) use these signals to reconstruct EEG-correlated representations with no EEG sensor on the victim. Per the abstract: perceived images inferred at 52.0 to 67.2% accuracy, activity fingerprinting above 85.0%, and de-anonymisation, gaze tracking and virtual keystroke inference above 96.0%, across several VR devices. NOT READ: participant numbers, class counts and chance levels, so the accuracies cannot yet be judged against baseline. What is inferred is a closed-set classification of stimulus or activity from a motion side channel; the study does not show decoding of arbitrary mental content. Defensive control: permission gating and rate limiting of motion sensors. Distinct from QIF-T0085 (optical eye tracking behind a permission) and QIF-T0087 (touchscreen tap tilt).

tara.mechanism: Inbuilt VR-headset motion sensors capture pupil-response-linked vibration; a learned model maps it to EEG-correlated representations used to classify perceived stimuli, activity, identity, gaze and virtual keystrokes

governance.safety_ceiling: Motion-sensor access gated by permission and rate limited; inference of perceptual or cognitive attributes from motion data requires explicit opt-in

Precedent cuts the other way: QIF-T0108 is DEMONSTRATED on two arXiv IDs. The rule's 'citation_unverified' flag is not present on any existing entry.

open_questions.question: Add seven techniques now, or hold?
open_questions.detail: The seven would take the catalogue from 165 to 172 with one DEMONSTRATED, two EMERGING on single preprints and four THEORETICAL on a review. The owner's Quorum 5.10 recommended holding new records for one batched migration.

open_questions.question: Who scopes the QIF-T0009 split?
open_questions.detail: M-S01 and M-C07 both wait on it. The split record for analog-front-end RF injection needs its own NISS and CVSS; the stored 7.4 belongs to the TMS-grade mechanism.

open_questions.question: Tactic choices
open_questions.detail: M-C02: M.SV (proposed) or N.IJ. M-C10: M.SV (proposed) or B.IN. M-C06: new record under M.SV (proposed) or a variant of QIF-T0109 under B.EV. M-C11: D.HV, since the catalogue has no exfiltration tactic.

open_questions.question: NISS convention for digital-only attacks
open_questions.detail: Scored on the newer convention (CR and CD separate; BI and RV only where tissue is affected; CV as consent over neural data or intent), all seven new techniques come out at 2.7 or below. On parity with the older M.SV family three of them would be 5.4 to 6.7. The two variants that inherit a parent vector keep 5.4 and 6.0. Decide whether to re-score QIF-T0016 to T0019 and QIF-T0024 or to keep family parity.

open_questions.question: Where does the malicious-aggregator case live?
open_questions.detail: Under the pipeline record (proposed) or as a companion entry to QIF-T0024 (Quorum 5.4).

open_questions.detail: Ni et al. 2026 (participants, class counts, chance levels); Cobilean et al. 2025 (attack success figures); Xie 2025 (over-the-air or simulated).

open_questions.detail: Hardware isolation failures (owner's item 6), output-based model inversion, sEMG as an interface modality, companion-device compromise, and the unassessed 'cognition and behaviour as an output channel'.

open_questions.question: PLAUSIBLE and SPECULATIVE
open_questions.detail: One entry each; outside the rubric and outside the TypeScript Status type. Fold into THEORETICAL or define them.

proposed_fields.note: Not added to any entry. Supports the fields already proposed in research-delta.json.

qtara-registrar.json techniques[].why: The rubric requires DEMONSTRATED entries to state dataset-level or hardware/participant; today that can only go in notes.
Three candidates are variants of existing entries with a lower evidence level than their parent; a structured sub-record would keep the variant's status from being read as the parent's.
A home for the rubric once agreed.

limits: The Bagley PDF was not available to this pass. The coverage matrix is built from the 22-vector summary in research-delta.json and from the section references in the owner's document.
Paper findings are taken from research-delta.json. Ten DOIs were re-resolved at Crossref in this session (metadata only); arXiv IDs were not re-fetched.

Duplicate checks used keyword search over attack, notes, tara.mechanism and sources for all 165 entries, followed by reading the nearest entries. 26 entries (QIF-T0136 to T0161) have no notes text and several others have empty notes, so those were judged from attack names and tara.mechanism.
Neurorights labels follow the registrar's taxonomy for threat-modelling purposes; the underlying concepts lack agreed operational definitions.

NISS scores describe signal-level and physical impact. The low scores for digital attacks are a property of the metric, not a statement that the attacks are unimportant; the catalogue's separate 'severity' field carries that judgement.
The Quorum validation step in the workspace research protocol was not run on this mapping.
